body:
This follow-up repairs the shell screen's command/argument boundaries while preserving exact-command approval for unparsed or computed code.

## Behavior

- Cmd `/c` and `/k` payloads are analyzed as complete commands. Literal text such as `echo ready for review` does not become an unfinished loop.
- FOR headers, parenthesized input sets, the actual `do` delimiter, and nonempty bodies are kept separate. A recursive root named `do` is data; missing delimiters and bodies require review.
- FOR /F file and literal-string inputs can pass screening. Command inputs still require explicit approval, including the backtick form selected by `usebackq`.
- Quoted POSIX `${@}`, slices/defaults of it, and `${!prefix@}` are not assumed to produce one field. This preserves the review boundary for computed `env`, `find`, and `fd` argument positions.
- Literal attached `fd` filters share recognition between screening and read-only classification. Real execution options remain mutable, and tests now require their screen verdict to be Clear rather than accepting a conservative fallback as evidence.
- Valid grouped `command` lookup switches and GNU `env`'s lone-dash option terminator preserve the executable boundary.

The external merge already imported POSIX wrapper/operand handling, executable-suffix checks, and fd permission classification. Those changes remain present; this follow-up repairs the review findings on that merged source. The public interface and tool implementation are unchanged by this two-file repair.

## Verification

Exact input head: `5be8cba8e9150be37b35dec47f2cace5647d704f`.
Candidate tree: `2dc5be64073c90b88fa0031c0f9b9c07e286831c`.

- Native observations were frozen before repair: 37 Cmd cases on Windows and 50 POSIX cases on Bash, Dash, GNU env, and fd.
- [Candidate preparation](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45950356366) authenticated both native archives, observed 53 mismatches among 97 frozen classifier expectations on the old source, then passed all 97 on the candidate. The exact pinned formatter and warning-clean compilation passed, and original source restoration was verified.
- [Current full proof](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45951139556): PENDING. Linux runs all three AGENTS gates after the required `rd` switch bootstrap. Windows repeats the complete frozen Cmd outputs and runs the actual tools-shell and permission suites after a full release build.
- The native permission test checks that blanket approval cannot run a command-source FOR /F loop or a bodyless loop, while explicit approval permits the benign command-source fixture.

The earlier Windows checkout failure and three initially incomplete stdout hypotheses remain recorded as failed historical runs. The complete Cmd echo traces are preserved in the replay oracle. The first preparation transport failure also remains separate; it occurred before any candidate application.

[Immutable proof checkpoint](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/blob/b0c2aa373c940621481b7e341925c3dbd7a1697b/ci-tools/charamel32-cmd/checkpoint.json).

## Earlier scope

The original PR addressed merged #30/#12 shell-screen feedback and retained computed-set coverage. Its earlier test result is historical evidence for that source, not a result for this externally merged revision. The CLI follow-up mentioned in the original body remains tracked by #26.

replies.text: The Cmd wrapper now reparses the complete literal /c or /k payload, preserving argument boundaries. The frozen old-source witness classifies `cmd /c echo ready for review` as Review; the candidate is Clear. Missing-do and bodyless payload controls remain Review. Exact source and required gate links will be attached after publication.

The parser recognizes `do` only after the parenthesized input set closes. Both quoted and unquoted recursive roots named `do` now remain data. Native Windows observations cover the root directory and the unchanged missing-body boundary; the old/candidate classifier pair is Review → Clear.

FOR /F now distinguishes file/literal inputs from command sources, including the quotation change made by the standalone `usebackq` option. File and literal inputs are Clear when their body is literal; single-quoted commands without usebackq and backtick commands with usebackq remain Review. Native fixtures and actual tool permission tests preserve explicit approval for those command sources.

The parameter-expansion path now clears the single-field proof for braced positional `@` and indirect prefix-`@` expansions. Native Bash/Dash records and classifier rows cover the quoted direct, sliced/default, and indirect forms, with scalar-transform, literal-@, and prefix-* controls retained. `env A="${@}" true` changes from Clear to Review.

Attached fd data-option recognition is shared by the execution scan and read-only classification. Native fd comparisons cover short attached and long equals forms. Plain attached searches are Clear/read-only; real -x/-X/--exec/--exec-batch actions remain recognized and mutable, including after an attached filter.

The command wrapper accepts fixed short-option groups containing only p/v/V before the terminator. A v or V selects lookup; p-only groups retain execution semantics. Bash/Dash observations and verdict controls cover grouped/separate forms, the terminator, invalid letters, computed operands, and executable suffixes.

Each existing literal fd execution-option row now asserts Shell_screen.Clear before asserting that the action is mutable. Attached-filter execution controls assert both properties too, so a conservative Review fallback cannot satisfy the test accidentally.

The PR description now includes the imported POSIX wrapper/operand, executable-suffix, and fd permission-classification scope, and separates the earlier source's evidence from the current exact-tree proof.

The env wrapper now consumes the lone '-' after recognized options and treats the following word as the command boundary. It does not resume option parsing afterward. Native tests use only an owned harmless executable stub; the frozen `env -i - ./cu''rl.exe` classifier witness changes from Clear to Blocked while the `env - -i ...` control preserves the literal '-i' executable boundary.
